teaching.hint: What does reaching one portal tell you about the cost of reaching the other portals with its letter?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Walking costs one and teleporting costs zero. A first minimum-distance arrival at a letter can make every portal of that letter available at the same distance; no later use can improve them.
solution_outline.approach: Group cells by letter and explore cells in nondecreasing move count, placing free teleports ahead of walking moves. Expand a letter's group only on its first settled encounter.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Store the best distance to each cell and which letters have been expanded. The next settled cell has minimum remaining distance; after a letter is expanded, every cell bearing it has been offered the smallest possible distance through that letter.
solution_outline.correctness: The distance order settles every cell at its minimum cost because each transition costs zero or one. Expanding the entire letter group at its first settled cell cannot lose a shorter route: any later arrival at that letter is no cheaper, and the first portal could already reach every destination in the group. Thus a minimum route satisfying the one-use rule is represented, including teleporting from the start.
solution_outline.complexity: O(mn) time and O(mn) space: each grid cell and walking edge is considered a constant number of times, and each letter group is expanded once.
solution_outline.pitfall: Ordinary FIFO exploration with a distance fixed on first discovery can commit to a walking route before a free teleport offers a shorter one.

accepted_alternatives: Dijkstra's algorithm over zero-cost portal edges and unit-cost walking edges is correct but adds a logarithmic factor.
common_wrong_turns: Track all used-letter subsets as path state
Scan all portals of a letter on every visit
Ignore a portal at the starting cell
source_fidelity_notes: The image-only example was omitted; the start-cell teleport rule was stated explicitly. Orthogonal movement, per-journey letter use, obstacles, dimensions, and unreachable result were retained.
